sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year from $129 billion in FY2017 to $303 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F203], while operating income grew 12.3% and net income 14.7% a year [F204][F205].
The window is steady compounding rather than a step change: revenue growth stayed between 5.0% and 17.5% every year [D336][D189], and the operating margin moved only from 3.2% to 3.9% [F23][F32].
FY2021 was the first inflection, with revenue up 17.5% [D189], as comparable sales rose 16% on stronger shopping frequency and average ticket and e-commerce comparable sales rose 44% [P54].
FY2022 was the second, revenue up 15.8% [D238], driven by a 14% comparable sales increase with gasoline, business centers and travel strongest and inflation above prior years [P42].
The United States is the growth engine, contributing +7.2pp of FY2026 revenue growth on a 72.5% share [D672][D670], with Other International adding +1.6pp and Canada +1.3pp [D679][D686].
FY2026 net sales rose $27.3 billion, or 10% [P14], primarily from an 8% comparable sales increase with average ticket up 5% and frequency up 3% [P14].
By product, Food and Sundries contributed +2.6pp and Non-Foods +2.2pp in FY2026 [D560][D576], while warehouse ancillary and other businesses jumped to +3.7pp on 19.9% growth [D601][D600].
Profit grew faster than revenue: FY2026 operating income rose 12.5% against 10.1% revenue growth [D435][D434], an incremental operating margin of 4.7% [D457].
Per-share growth tracked net income closely, diluted EPS up 14.0% against net income up 13.9% [D438][D436], because the diluted share count was essentially flat at 444.4 million [X100][D452].
The FY2026 operating margin of 3.9% is the window high, against a 3.4% median and a 3.1% low in FY2019 [F32][D691][D692][D690].
The latest year added only +0.1pp [D447], with SG&A contributing +0.1pp and cost of revenue flat [D460][D459].
SG&A fell 10 basis points as a share of sales, though excluding gasoline price inflation it rose one basis point, with foreign currency adding $126 million of expense [P9].
Gross margin fell three basis points, but excluding gasoline inflation it rose 10 basis points, helped by a sales mix shift toward warehouse ancillary and IEEPA tariff refunds [P12].
Below the line, the 24.7% effective tax rate [D420] left net margin at 3.0% [F52], a record high against a 2.6% median [D694][D695].
FY2026 operating cash flow of $15.8 billion was 1.71x net income [F82][D421], and free cash flow of $9.4 billion was 1.02x [F102][D422], above the 0.99x window median [D701].
The 18.6% operating cash flow increase came from higher operating income and a reduced net investment in inventories from faster turns and improved supplier payment terms [D439][P6].
Free cash flow margin was 3.1% [D418], below the 3.6% window high in FY2020 [D697], as capex rose 17.0% to $6.4 billion [D441][F92].
Capital intensity is rising: capex was 2.1% of revenue and 2.41x D&A in FY2026 [D417][D423], the highest multiple in the window [D11].
Net cash reached $15.1 billion, or 5.0% of revenue [D427][D428], the 100th percentile against retail peers whose median is -4.4% of revenue (n=6) [D715][D716].
Cash and investments rose 39.4% to $21.3 billion [D453][D425] while total debt grew 6.5% to $6.2 billion [D454][D426], and the current ratio was 1.06x [F182].
Financing outflow was $3.4 billion [F122], mainly dividends, buybacks and debt repayment [P4], with $848 million of repurchases [X110] and $2.5 billion of dividends [X120].
Capital return was only 35.2% of free cash flow [D430], so the share count barely moved, down 0.1% [D452], and equity grew 22.8% [D444].
Margins remain thin against peers: operating margin sits at the 17th percentile versus a 5.0% retail median (n=6) [D709][D710], and net margin is also 17th percentile against 3.5% [D711][D712].
Capex has outgrown depreciation for years, with the capex/D&A ratio at 2.41x [D423], so free cash flow depends on continued sales leverage to absorb the build.
Receivables grew 23.6% in FY2026 [D455], faster than the 10.1% revenue growth [D434], lifting days sales outstanding to 5 days from 4 [D431][D382].
The pack lists no red-flag candidates (section E is empty), so these are drawn from the filed lines and derived ratios rather than flagged items.
Operating margin: a FY2027 print below the 3.4% window median [D692] would reverse the climb from 3.2% in FY2017 [F23], and it will appear in the FY2027 10-K.
Free cash flow conversion: a ratio below the 0.99x window median [D701] would signal capex outrunning cash generation, reported in the FY2027 cash flow statement.
Net cash: a fall below the FY2025 level of $9.5 billion [D378] would mark the first reversal of the build, visible in the FY2027 balance sheet.
